title: In later geological periods new species have roughly balanced extinctions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: In later geological periods new species have roughly balanced extinctions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The number of species has not increased indefinitely, at least in the later geological periods, so the production of new forms has caused the extinction of about the same number of old forms.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: so that looking to later times we may believe that the production of new forms has caused the extinction of about the same number of old forms.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “On Extinction”. Scope: global species diversity in later geological periods

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing data can test approximate numerical balance over selected periods. They have much less power to establish Darwin's causal interpretation or a global species-level ceiling.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate sampling-standardized global diversity, origination, and extinction rates across later geological intervals. Test whether long-run net diversification is near zero and whether origination covaries with losses, while separating balance from causation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rate balance does not show that new forms caused extinctions.

Global species richness is incompletely sampled.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.59
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.76
data existence: 0.89
analysis feasibility: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Origination, extinction, and standing diversity are the right variables and are already compiled. The scientific disagreement that remains is largely about sampling and rock volume, which means the same public data do not yet yield one decisive balance test. A restricted marine, genus-level version of the question is analyzable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare sampling-standardized origination and extinction counts, and the trend in standing diversity, through the Cenozoic and other later Phanerozoic intervals. Matched gains and losses with flat diversity would support a balance; a sustained rise in diversity would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Later geological periods is an elastic interval, and global species richness is not observed directly.

Different standardizations still disagree about whether later diversity is flat or rising.

fields.label: Dimension scores

analysis feasibility: 0.75
